instructions: Rinse the 1 1/2 cups rice in a sieve under cold water until it runs mostly clear. Add it to a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups water and bring it to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on for 10 minutes. No peeking.

If the shrimp are frozen, thaw them in a bowl of cold water for about 10 minutes. Peel and devein them if they aren't already. Pat them very dry with paper towels, transfer them to a bowl and toss with 2 tbsp of the wine and 2 tsp of the cornstarch.
Meanwhile, cut the broccoli into small florets. Mince the 4 garlic cloves and 1 tbsp of the ginger. Slice 2 of the scallions thinly.
In a small bowl, stir together 1/2 cup water, the doubanjiang, soy sauce, the last 1 tbsp wine and the ground Szechuan peppercorns. In a cup, stir the last 1 tsp cornstarch into 1 tsp cold water.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high. Add the broccoli and 1/4 cup water, cover and cook for 2 minutes. Uncover and cook for 1 minute, until the water has cooked off and the broccoli is bright green. Transfer it to a plate.

Add 2 tbsp oil to the pan and let it heat for 30 seconds. Add the shrimp in one layer and stir for 3 to 4 minutes, until they're pink and curl into a loose C. Transfer them to the plate with the broccoli.
Turn the heat to medium and add the last 1 tbsp oil. Add the ginger and stir for 30 seconds. Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant and hasn't browned.
Stir the sauce and pour it in. Bring it to a boil and cook for 1 to 2 minutes.

Return the shrimp, the broccoli and any juices from the plate. Bring the sauce back to a boil, then stir the cornstarch mix and pour it in. Stir for 1 to 2 minutes, until the sauce is glossy and thick and the shrimp are hot all the way through.
Take the pan off the heat and scatter the scallions over the top.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with the rice, and put the chili oil on the table for anyone who wants heat.
method_notes: All Ways Delicious (the lead) marinates the shrimp in Shaoxing wine and cornstarch, sears them and sets them aside, cooks garlic and ginger, then builds a quick sauce of doubanjiang, soy, wine and Szechuan pepper and thickens it with a cornstarch slurry. China Sichuan Food leans harder on dried chilies and whole Sichuan peppercorns; Craving Tasty adds broccoli and bell peppers. This follows the lead, with the doubanjiang cut to 1 tbsp, the chili oil moved to the table (use one made without peanuts) and broccoli added from the Craving Tasty version. The 30 minutes includes the rice.
